{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Co-Development and Funding Agreement (Execution Version)

**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side — "PB")  
**Re:** Playbook review findings, SFJ co-development / funding agreement  
**Status:** 18 rules assessed — 5 deviations, 11 compliant, 2 requiring manual review

## Executive summary

We have reviewed the execution version against our playbook. The commercial architecture (success-contingent Approval Payments, no minimum purchase, no exclusivity or non-compete on us, no SFJ audit right, and a strong post-termination transition and data-return regime in Article 14.3) sits at or above our preferred positions and needs no redlining.

The exposure is concentrated in the exit and liability provisions. Three items are in walk-away territory: (i) Section 14.2.1's 300% of Development Costs payable by us on SFJ's termination for our breach, expressly "in lieu of any claim for damages" (Section 14.4.2); (ii) Section 14.2.6's SFJ sole-discretion right to terminate on a Change of Control of PB plus a 150% payment, which undercuts the M&A carve-out we obtained in Section 15.6; and (iii) Section 14.2.10's SFJ sole-discretion termination on continued disagreement with a decision we are contractually entitled to make, with Development Costs plus 25% interest. In parallel, our own at-will right in Section 14.2.2 is gated behind $60 million of SFJ spend and closes at first Regulatory Approval, leaving us without a convenience exit for much of a multi-year program.

Two further gaps require attention. Section 15.11 excludes indirect damages but sets **no aggregate monetary cap** for either party, leaving our direct-damages exposure under the broad Article 12 indemnities unlimited. And the Article 12 IP allocation runs one way: SFJ's indemnity at 12.1.1 has no IP element, while ours at 12.1.2(f) covers infringement "by either Party in performing its duties or obligations hereunder" — we indemnify SFJ for infringement caused by SFJ's own performance. Article 11.3.2 confirms no counterparty IP indemnity sits elsewhere. Separately, SFJ performs real services (global CRO oversight and trial execution) with no performance warranty behind them, and the all-caps disclaimer at 13.6.2 carves out only what is "set forth in this Article 13."

Finally, the ownership-of-deliverables (IP) and licence-grant-scope rules did not complete automated review and must be worked manually before we sign off.

## Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Deviation | Indemnification and Insurance (12.1.1, 12.1.2(f); cf. 11.3.2) |
| 2 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | **Needs review** | — (automated review incomplete) |
| 3 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | Term and Termination (14.2.6; cf. 15.6, 6.7.2) |
| 4 | High | LD — Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer | Deviation | Term and Termination (14.2.1; 14.4.2) |
| 5 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | **Needs review** | — (automated review incomplete) |
| 6 | High | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability: cap, mutuality, carve-outs | Deviation | 15.11 (cf. Article 12, 13.6) |
| 7 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Deviation | Term and Termination (14.2.2; 14.2.10) |
| 8 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant | 3.19 (with 1.1.68) |
| 9 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete restrictions on Customer | Compliant | 3.19; Article 7 (7.5.1–7.5.7) |
| 10 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Deviation | Representations and Warranties (13.5; 13.6.2; cf. 3.1.4, 3.1.5) |
| 11 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | Records (9.1, 9.2; cf. 3.6, 7.6) |
| 12 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | 15.9; 15.10 (15.10.2.2) |
| 13 | Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations | Compliant | Security Interest (7.4; cf. 7.5.5) |
| 14 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | Compliant | Development Costs (Article 6, 6.2, 6.7; 4.2.3) |
| 15 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Compliant (fallback) | 15.16 |
| 16 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice | Compliant | Term and Termination (14.1; 1.1.60) |
| 17 | Medium | TRANSITION — Post-termination transition and data return | Compliant | Term and Termination (14.3.1–14.3.5; 11.1.1.4; 10.3) |
| 18 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Compliant | Indemnification and Insurance (12.3.1–12.3.4) |

### Notes on the deviations and our proposals

- **INDEMN (12.1.1 / 12.1.2(f)):** Add an SFJ IP-infringement indemnity for SFJ's own activities and narrow our IP indemnity so it no longer covers SFJ's performance. We keep our indemnity for the Product and our own performance, which is appropriate since we own and supply the Product.
- **ASSIGN (14.2.6):** Delete SFJ's right to terminate on a PB Change of Control and the related 150% payment, retaining our notice obligation. Section 15.6 is already at or above our preferred position (mutual, Affiliate and successor assignments permitted, including reverse triangular mergers); 14.2.6 undercuts it.
- **LD (14.2.1):** Reduce the 300% multiple to a return of Development Costs actually paid or incurred — the same measure the parties already agreed in Section 14.2.9. We take the fallback here rather than press for no customer-payable amount, given SFJ funds the trials. Related penalty mechanics we would expect to align on the same basis: the 25% interest uplift (14.2.10) and the 150% multiples (14.2.6, 14.2.8.1).
- **LOL-CAP (15.11):** Insert a mutual aggregate cap at the greater of 12 months' payments between the parties and USD 1,000,000, with uncapped carve-outs for confidentiality/data security, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement, and expressly preserving our Article 6 / Section 14.2 payment obligations outside the cap.
- **T4C (14.2.2 / 14.2.10):** Ungate our at-will right (30 days' notice, no $60M spend threshold) and delete SFJ's sole-discretion termination on JSC disagreement with its payment consequence. We accept the 300% exit payment in 14.2.2 as the priced return in this funding bargain rather than press the preferred no-penalty position.
- **WARRANTY (13.5):** Add an SFJ performance warranty for the SFJ Services (workmanlike standard, SFJ SOPs, Protocol, Applicable Law including GCP and ICH) with re-performance at SFJ's cost, excluded from Development Costs. We inserted it into 13.5 so it falls automatically within the 13.6.2 carve-out; no fixed warranty period is proposed because these are continuous trial-conduct obligations.

## Walk-away items

These three provisions are identified in the findings as walk-away territory and should not be conceded without escalation:

1. **Section 14.2.1 (with 14.4.2)** — 300% of all Development Costs paid or incurred, accelerated on SFJ's termination for our material breach and standing "in lieu of any claim for damages," payable regardless of whether Regulatory Approval is ever obtained. This can exceed the value remaining to us under the Agreement.
2. **Section 14.2.6** — SFJ's sole-discretion right to terminate the entire Agreement on a Change of Control of PB, plus a 150% of Development Costs payment. A vendor right to terminate or re-price on our change of control is an express walk-away.
3. **Section 14.2.10** — SFJ's "sole discretion," immediate-notice termination triggered by its continued disagreement with a decision we are contractually entitled to make, with Development Costs plus 25% interest payable by us.

## Next steps

1. **Complete the two open rules.** Manually review ownership of deliverables and Customer Data (IP) and licence grant scope (LICENSE); automated review failed on both and neither has a verified position. No sign-off until these close.
2. **Issue the redlines** on the five deviations as drafted above, leading with the three walk-away provisions in Article 14 and the Section 15.11 cap.
3. **Confirm the redactions.** Obtain the unredacted figures for: insurance limits under 12.3.2 (against USD 1M/2M CGL and USD 2M E&O); the non-solicit tail period in 15.16 (target 12 months or less from the end of the individual's involvement; revisit anything above 24 months); and the transition and delivery periods in 14.3.3–14.3.4 (against the 6-month/30-day benchmarks).
4. **Confirm position on the Program Transfer path.** Section 14.3 applies only if SFJ has not triggered a Program Transfer under Section 3.20; the Exhibit O Program Transfer Agreement should be reviewed under the change-of-control/remedies rules.
5. **Hold the line on the compliant items.** In particular, resist any SFJ attempt to introduce an audit or inspection right; if one is introduced, we would require it be limited to once per 12 months on 30 days' notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, at SFJ's cost absent a >5% discrepancy, with no direct access to our systems.
6. **Noted, not flagged (for awareness only):** Delaware law in 15.9 sits at our fallback rather than the preferred New York choice, and 15.10 uses domestic ICDR arbitration (New York seat, FAA-governed) rather than New York County courts. The Section 7.5.5 Licensing Transaction consent gate is a financing covenant we are treating under the negative-covenant rules, not as exclusivity or non-compete. Section 12.3 has no express cyber/privacy liability line.
"}
